messages.text: Gurney called up to World Series Finals after withdrawals due to visa issues

metadata.summary: Daryl Gurney has been called up to play at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam after visa issues led to the withdrawal of Philippines players Lourence Ilagan and Alexis Toylo from the September 17-20 event.
metadata.content: World Series of Darts Finals: 2026 schedule and results with Luke Littler, Luke Humphries, Michael van Gerwen, Gian van Veen in action | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to content World Series of Darts Finals: 2026 schedule and results with Luke Littler, Luke Humphries, Michael van Gerwen, Gian van Veen in action A top prize of £100,000 will be up for grabs at the 2026 World Series of Darts Finals featuring a blockbuster 32-player field, with tournament to commence on September 17 in Amsterdam Wednesday 9 September 2026 19:43, UK Image: Daryl Gurney will play reigning champion Michael van Gerwen in round one Daryl Gurney has been called up to play at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam after visa issues led to the withdrawal of Philippines players Lourence Ilagan and Alexis Toylo from the September 17-20 event. Northern Ireland's Gurney and the Netherlands' Maik Kuivenhoven were the highest-ranked players on the reserve list and have replaced Ilagan and Toylo respectively after the pair did not receive a decision on their Schengen visa applications before having to travel to China this week for the final two events of the PDC Asian Tour season. Gurney will face reigning tournament champion and home favourite Michael van Gerwen in the first round at AFAS Live on Thursday September 17, while Kuivenhoven plays Jonny Clayton the following day. messages.text: Prince William launches suicide prevention toolkit for sport

metadata.summary: Prince William will bring together leading figures from across sport on Thursday to launch a new first-of-its-kind suicide prevention toolkit designed to help organisations recognise warning signs and support those at risk.
metadata.content: Prince William launches landmark suicide prevention toolkit for sport on World Suicide Prevention Day | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to content Prince William launches landmark suicide prevention toolkit for sport on World Suicide Prevention Day Prince William to launch new suicide prevention toolkit for sport; Dame Kelly Holmes, Jill Scott, Gabby Logan, Campbell Hatton and Dame Laura Kenny among sporting figures backing initiative; FA, Premier League, British Cycling and Team GB committed to implementing toolkit Wednesday 9 September 2026 17:48, UK Image: Prince William Prince William will bring together leading figures from across sport on Thursday to launch a new first-of-its-kind suicide prevention toolkit designed to help organisations recognise warning signs and support those at risk. The landmark event will take place at Everton's Hill Dickinson Stadium in Liverpool on World Suicide Prevention Day, September 10. Dame Kelly Holmes, Gabby Logan, Campbell Hatton, Jill Scott and Dame Laura Kenny are among those joining the Prince of Wales at the launch of 'On Your Side' . The toolkit, developed by The Royal Foundation in partnership with the British Standards Institution and mental health charity Chasing the Stigma, aims to turn suicide prevention into everyday practice across the sporting sector.
